source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)

coverage.scope: B.1 Proof of Claims and Process; B.2 Grounds for Disallowance, limitations, lease and employee damage caps, §502(k); Problem 5.2(a)-(f) unanswered
coverage.notice: Time limits and form rules as described in supplied 2021 text, subject to applicable Rules/Code changes after book edition.

topics.title: B.1 — From Claim to Allowed Claim: Proofs, Notices, Deadlines, Objections
topics.description: Formal allowance pathway §501/§502, chapter differences, timely versus late claims and estimation.

entries.title: Three distinct statuses: claim, allowed claim, discharge
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: A right to payment may be a §101(5) claim; to share distributions or vote, claim must generally be allowed under §§501–502; a claim can be discharged even without being allowed.
entries.laymanExplanation: A creditor may hold real debt but miss a payout filing; discharge questions don't entirely depend on payout.
entries.legalExplanation: Chapter 7 no-asset cases frequently have no unsecured distributions, so filing proof often unnecessary unless notice requests it.
entries.examApplication: If asked who gets money, determine validity, proof/deemed filing and §502 objections separately.
entries.examTrap: Disallowance of a claim for distribution does not always mean debt discharged; unpaid debt not necessarily survives.

entries.title: §501 / Rule 3001: proof of claim
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Ordinarily a creditor files Official Form 410 or substantially compliant written statement setting out its claim with court clerk; claim holder or indenture trustee usually files.
entries.laymanExplanation: Proof of claim is the application to participate in bankruptcy creditor payouts.
entries.legalExplanation: Rules 3001(a), 3002(b), 5005; supporting documents and evidentiary effect depend on compliance.
entries.examApplication: Start at whether creditor filed and by applicable date; no-asset case exceptions.
entries.examTrap: Simply listing creditor on debtor's schedules doesn't satisfy rules in every chapter.

entries.title: Debtor/trustee/cosigner can sometimes file for creditor
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: If creditor doesn't timely file, debtor, trustee or entity liable with debtor may file under §501(b),(c) and Rule 3004 in limited circumstances.
entries.laymanExplanation: Debtor may want nondischargeable child support creditor to get estate money to reduce surviving balance.
entries.legalExplanation: Person with economic stake in distribution can protect against creditor neglect.
entries.examApplication: Look for §523 nondischargeable obligation; debtor wants share applied before later collection.
entries.examTrap: Not unrestricted right of strangers to file any claim anytime.

entries.title: §1111(a): Chapter 11 schedule can deem proof filed
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Chapter 11 creditor with correctly scheduled noncontingent, liquidated and undisputed claim need not file separately; disputed/contingent/unliquidated or misvalued claims require creditor proof.
entries.laymanExplanation: Chapter 11 list itself can count as the application if debtor admits fixed debt.
entries.examApplication: Identify exact scheduled amount and whether marked disputed, contingent or unliquidated.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply Chapter 11 deemed-filing shortcut to Chapter 7.

entries.title: Notice to creditors, bar date and §342
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Debtor files creditor schedules; notices include meeting and proof date. Section 342 specifies effective notice to institutional creditors that designate service address/account number. Inadequate notice may protect claims from discharge.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank must get bankruptcy notice through proper address/department when legally designated.
entries.legalExplanation: §523(a)(3) protects unscheduled/no-notice claims in specified individual contexts; corporate discharge demands due process notice.
entries.examApplication: Check whether claimant knew case in time, official notice address and whether proper filing chance.
entries.examTrap: Do not assume mail to any random corporate branch is always effective.

entries.title: General Chapter 7, 12, 13 bar dates (book Rules)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: As set out in uploaded textbook, Rule 3002(c) generally requires proof within 70 days after petition for voluntary cases, or 90 days after order for relief in involuntary cases; exceptions apply.
entries.laymanExplanation: Ordinary creditors have deadlines counted from filing/order—use correct start.
entries.legalExplanation: Textbook is 2021; current procedures may require updated Rules, but for book hypothetical use assigned wording.
entries.examApplication: Show calendar starting with voluntary petition or involuntary order for relief and count 70/90 days.
entries.examTrap: Don't use old ‘90 days after creditors meeting’ general rule.

entries.title: Government claim timing
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Under §502(b)(9), governmental unit general claim deadline in book is 180 days from order for relief; particular Chapter 13 tax proof may be within 60 days after return filed.
entries.laymanExplanation: Tax agency has a different timer from ordinary private creditor.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish government and tax-return special timing.
entries.examApplication: In mixed problem write government-specific deadline instead of ordinary 70 days.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume every tax claim follows a 70-day timer.

entries.title: Chapter 11 flexible court-set bar dates and excusable neglect
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Chapter 11 court sets deadline under Rule 3003(c)(3) and may extend for cause, including excusable neglect under Rule 9006(b)(1) and Pioneer.
entries.laymanExplanation: Long corporate restructuring may need flexible creditor filing schedule.
entries.legalExplanation: Different from automatic Rule 3002 general date; notice and due process critical.
entries.examApplication: Identify whether court entered bar-date order and creditor missed deadline due to excuse.
entries.examTrap: Not blanket right to submit late whenever creditor wants.

entries.title: Late priority versus general unsecured distribution
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: §502(b)(9) timeliness rule has §726 exceptions: late priority proof may remain in first tier before final report/distribution cutoff; late nonpriority without notice may get second-tier payment if proof timely enough for distribution; ordinary other late claims third tier.
entries.laymanExplanation: Late creditor isn't always totally barred, but often moves down line.
entries.legalExplanation: Section 726(a)(1),(2)(C),(3) determine tiers, whereas §502(b)(9) acknowledges exceptions.
entries.examApplication: For tardy claim ask priority category, notice, when filed and when trustee distributions started.
entries.examTrap: Don't categorically disallow every late proof or put every late general claim in tier 2.

entries.title: §502(a): filed proof deemed allowed absent objection
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Proof filed under §501 is deemed allowed unless party in interest objects; compliant proof has prima facie evidentiary effect (Rule 3001(f)).
entries.laymanExplanation: No one challenges claim? Normally it can participate without lawsuit.
entries.legalExplanation: Trustee must examine and object to improper claims under §704(a)(5); others with stake may object.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish automatic allowance from contested objection and burden rules.
entries.examTrap: Filing proof is not unchallengeable judgment in creditor's favor.

entries.title: Contested proofs: §502(b), §502(c) and forums
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: On objection, court determines validity/amount at petition date under §502(b); contingent or unliquidated claims must be estimated if liquidation delays administration, §502(c); claims objection generally core under 28 USC §157(b)(2)(B), but personal injury/wrongful death estimation/liquidation special process.
entries.laymanExplanation: Judge might estimate an uncertain asbestos damages claim so estate can pay now.
entries.legalExplanation: The system can't exclude uncertain claims as unprovable like old law did.
entries.examApplication: Ask if claim can be liquidated promptly or estimation necessary; identify proper judicial forum.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume bankruptcy judge conducts full jury trial on personal injury amount.

entries.title: Burden rules from underlying law (Raleigh)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Although Rule 3001(f) provides prima facie case for compliant proof, after objection underlying nonbankruptcy law ordinarily supplies burdens of persuasion/production under Raleigh v Illinois DOR.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bankruptcy filing doesn't automatically reverse ordinary burden of proving debt.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish filing presumption and ultimate burden on state tax/contract claim.
entries.examApplication: If objection challenges legally invalid contract, use relevant contract-law burden.
entries.examTrap: Raleigh is cited but not fully excerpted opinion.

entries.title: Reconsideration and settlement of claim
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Order allowing/disallowing claim may be reconsidered for cause §502(j), Rule 3008; compromise under Rule 9019(a) generally requires court approval following creditor notice.
entries.laymanExplanation: A disputed claim can be settled, but trustee generally needs judge approval.
entries.legalExplanation: Withdrawal Rule 3006 ordinarily available before objection/significant participation; recheck procedure.
entries.examApplication: If creditor and trustee compromise amount, don't skip approval requirements.
entries.examTrap: Not every phone agreement between creditor and trustee changes allowed amount.

topics.title: B.2 — §502(b) Grounds for Disallowance: Three Categories
topics.description: Timing, underlying legal enforceability and bankruptcy-specific policy grounds including (d),(e),(k).

entries.title: §502 disallowance grounds are statutory and exclusive
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: After objection, disallowance rests on §502(b)(1)–(9) plus §§502(d),(e),(k), not court's free-floating fairness determination.
entries.laymanExplanation: Court can't refuse valid claim solely because creditor seems rich or unsympathetic.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish equitable subordination under §510(c) from §502 disallowance.
entries.examApplication: Start §502(b) text and relevant exception rather than broad morality.
entries.examTrap: A valid claim can be subordinated without being disallowed.

entries.title: Timing: amount measured as of filing; later exceptions
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: §502(b) fixes petition-date amount; new postpetition obligation generally not ordinary prepetition allowed claim. Exceptions: §502(g) postpetition contract rejection treated as prepetition, §502(h) avoidance recovery claim similarly.
entries.laymanExplanation: New fraud after filing is usually not old creditor claim; rejection damages treated specially.
entries.legalExplanation: Contingent and unmatured already prepetition are not disallowed simply because future payment date.
entries.examApplication: For 5.2(b) identify fraud June1 AFTER May1 filing; for contracts separate preexisting obligations.
entries.examTrap: Do not equate contingent future maturity with postpetition origin.

entries.title: §502(b)(1): enforceability defenses carry over
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: If claim unenforceable under applicable agreement/nonbankruptcy law for reason other than contingency/unmaturity, disallow to same extent; examples expired statute of limitations and contract defenses.
entries.laymanExplanation: Expired warranty lawsuit doesn't become revived just because seller went bankrupt.
entries.legalExplanation: §558 lets estate assert debtor's defenses; limitations date measured properly under UCC, subject relevant law exceptions.
entries.examApplication: In 5.2(a) compare 2014 gizmo sale and 2020 proof with four-year UCC warranty limit.
entries.examTrap: Bankruptcy generally does not create new cause of action.

entries.title: §502(b)(2): unmatured/postpetition interest excluded
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Unsecured claim cannot include unaccrued interest after filing; claim amount fixed petition date. Exceptions include oversecured §506(b) postpetition interest to collateral surplus and solvent Chapter 7 §726(a)(5) interest tier.
entries.laymanExplanation: Loan continues accruing contract interest in ordinary world, but bankruptcy claim usually freezes at filing.
entries.legalExplanation: Compute principal and accrued interest through petition, not all future contracted interest; interest already accrued prefiling is included if enforceable.
entries.examApplication: For 5.2(c) identify each loan rate/interest paid through Dec2019, Jan1 filing; for 5.2(d) separate $5k principal and $6k 2022 payoff.
entries.examTrap: Do not award all $6k future amount solely because contract promises it.

entries.title: §502(b)(3),(4),(5),(8),(9), (d),(e) overview
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Disallowance includes excess tax against estate asset value (b)(3); excessive insider/attorney service fees (b)(4); specified unmatured future support (b)(5); employment tax adjustment (b)(8); late proofs (b)(9); transferee failing turnover of avoidable transfer (d); contingent reimbursement/contribution/subrogation (e).
entries.laymanExplanation: Code has numerous specialized reasons to limit otherwise valid demands.
entries.legalExplanation: Each belongs statute rather than flexible equitable power; apply precise predicates.
entries.examApplication: List subsection in any atypical claim question, especially tax, insiders, avoidable transfers.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume all support or tax claims disallowed; narrow subsection requirements.

entries.title: §502(k): refusal to negotiate consumer debt proposal
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Court may reduce qualifying consumer debt claim up to 20% if creditor unreasonably refuses to consider approved nonprofit counselor's proposal ≥60 days before petition to pay ≥60% over reasonable time; clear-and-convincing proof, no §523(a) nondischargeability portion.
entries.laymanExplanation: Credit card lender might lose up to fifth of claim for improperly ignoring timely good-faith debt workout offer.
entries.legalExplanation: Proof predicates are narrow and user must prove refusal, not just creditor declining different payment.
entries.examApplication: Calculate 20% × allowed principal if all conditions, but exclude nondischargeable debt.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply §502(k) without accredited counselor and offer timing/minimum.

topics.title: B.2 — §502(b)(6) Real Property Lease Rejection Damages Cap
topics.description: Step-by-step calculation, 12-month floor, 36-month ceiling, rent arrears, actual damages and exceptions.

entries.title: Landlord cap formula: greater of one year or 15% up to three years
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: §502(b)(6)(A) cap on lease-termination damages for REAL property: reserved rent over maximum of (12 months, min(15% of remaining term,36 months)), PLUS separate unpaid pretermination rent subject §502(b)(6)(B). Actual enforceable damages can be less.
entries.laymanExplanation: Landlord can't claim all 99 years of unpaid future rent ahead of other creditors.
entries.legalExplanation: Calculate 15% in months; apply at least 12 and at most 36; multiply by monthly reserved rent, add eligible unpaid rent; compare actual mitigated claim.
entries.examApplication: For 5.2(e) 91-year remaining term yields 36-month ceiling; but actual $50k/year difference after relet may matter.
entries.examTrap: The ceiling is not guaranteed award. Don't confuse separate back rent with future cap.

entries.title: Quick calculation: 5 years remaining
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: 60 months × 0.15 = 9 months, floor 12 months. At $100,000 annual rent, capped future amount is $100,000 before separately qualifying arrears.
entries.laymanExplanation: Five years left still only one year's rent allowed at most.
entries.legalExplanation: Threshold remaining 80 months produces 12 months; under 80 months floor controls.
entries.examApplication: Write 60×.15=9 < 12 → 12 months.
entries.examTrap: Do not calculate 15% × annual rent; multiply percentage by remaining TERM.

entries.title: Quick calculation: 10 years remaining
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: 120 months ×0.15=18 months; between 12 and 36; at $100k annual rent, maximum future damages $150k.
entries.laymanExplanation: Ten-year lease may get 1.5 years of rent as cap.
entries.legalExplanation: Rent reserved basis distinct from loss after mitigation.
entries.examTrap: Do not round 18 months to 2 years.

entries.title: Quick calculation: 20+ years remaining
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: 240 months ×0.15=36 months; 20+ years hits cap 3 years. At $100k annual rent, future loss ceiling $300k plus qualifying prepetition rent.
entries.laymanExplanation: Hundred-year lease doesn't give decades of rent priority; at most 36-month future rent cap.
entries.legalExplanation: Long leases beyond 20 years stay at 36-month threshold.
entries.examApplication: Problem 5.2(e): 91 remaining years, compute 36 months at $100k/year $300k ceiling; must compare lower actual lost spread.
entries.examTrap: 15% of 91 years isn't the final permitted cap due to 36-month maximum.

entries.title: Actual losses and mitigation can be less than statutory ceiling
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: A capped claim is min(actual enforceable damages under contract/state law after mitigation, statutory max). Landlord may relet premises and reduce harm.
entries.laymanExplanation: If tenant broke lease but landlord replaced tenant, landlord can't necessarily collect entire ceiling if real loss smaller.
entries.legalExplanation: §502(b)(1) disallows underlying legally avoidable/massively mitigated damages; §502(b)(6) upper limit independently applies.
entries.examApplication: For 5.2(e) compare $100k old rent vs $50k new across 91 years, mitigation and potential discount, then 3-year cap.
entries.examTrap: Never assume statutory cap amount itself is the actual claim amount.

entries.title: Assumed and later rejected lease — §503(b)(7) special rule
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Where estate assumed nonresidential real estate lease then rejects, §503(b)(7) gives administrative expense for sums due during two years after rejection (or surrender if later) subject to relet mitigation; later-term damages as prepetition claim subject §502(b)(6).
entries.laymanExplanation: If bankruptcy estate chose to keep lease and later abandoned it, special post-assumption payment rules apply.
entries.legalExplanation: Important exception to ordinary prepetition §502 cap for initial administrative period.
entries.examApplication: Identify whether contract rejected immediately or assumed first; nonresidential premises.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply ordinary §502(b)(6) limit to all §503 administrative expense amounts.

topics.title: B.2 — §502(b)(7) Employment Contract Termination Cap
topics.description: Separate from §507(a)(4) wage priority; employee contract damages ceiling.

entries.title: §502(b)(7) cap for future employee termination compensation
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: Allow employee termination damages only up to contract compensation for ONE YEAR after earlier of petition or performance termination, without acceleration, plus unpaid compensation due at that earlier date.
entries.laymanExplanation: Baseball player can't necessarily collect every year of ten-year $25m contract after team folds.
entries.legalExplanation: Contractual salary one-year ceiling distinct from §507(a)(4) much smaller wage priority cap; claim still may be general unsecured.
entries.examApplication: For 5.2(f) 10-year $25m/year contract, identify earlier date, calculate up to $25m one-year future compensation plus eligible past due amounts, leaving outcome unanswered.
entries.examTrap: Do not confuse size of allowed employee claim with amount qualifying for wage priority.

entries.title: Employee claim allowance vs priority are separate numerical questions
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: §502(b)(7) caps allowed termination-damages claim; §507(a)(4),(5) determine smaller priority treatment for wages/benefits earned within 180-day window and capped per employee (source-era indexed dollars).
entries.laymanExplanation: Allowed $25m claim doesn't imply $25m paid before general unsecured creditors.
entries.legalExplanation: First allow claim, THEN allocate priority share, THEN distribute as estate permits.
entries.examApplication: For athlete hypothetical make two columns, allowed damages vs priority if any.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply wage-priority amount as if it were maximum total claim.

topics.title: B.2 — Problem 5.2(a)–(f): Allowance and Calculations (Unsolved)
topics.description: All six scenarios preserved without supplied conclusions.

entries.title: No-answer computational issue-spotting checklist
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
entries.summary: For each scenario write (1) date claim legally arose, (2) nonbankruptcy enforceability, (3) statutory disallowance subsection, (4) permitted dollar claim at petition, and (5) any separate priority issue.
entries.laymanExplanation: Don't decide by how unfair creditor appears; do the math and statutory classification.
entries.legalExplanation: Keep original 5.2(a)–(f) unanswered, with formulas available elsewhere in notes.
entries.examApplication: Apply §502(b)(1),(2),(6),(7) and petition date carefully.
entries.examTrap: An unliquidated allowed claim ≠ no claim.

problems.title: Problem 5.2(a)
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
problems.prompt: Buyer purchased gizmo from debtor in 2014; debtor Chapter 7 in 2020; buyer first alleges defective product via proof of claim; UCC Article 2 warranty limitations four years from tender. Decide disallowance under §502(b)(1); unanswered.

problems.title: Problem 5.2(b)
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
problems.prompt: Debtor filed Chapter 7 May 1, 2020; on June 1 debtor commits new fraud by selling pirated DVD as authentic; victim claims refund through bankruptcy proof. Identify postpetition timing versus allowed prepetition claim; unanswered.

problems.title: Problem 5.2(c)
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
problems.prompt: Creditor A: Jan1 2018 $1,000 loan at 10% annual; creditor B: Jan1 2019 $1,000 at 8%; both only interest paid through Dec31 2019; debtor filed Jan1 2020 when market rate 8%. Identify allowed principal and which interest may be included under §502(b)(2); unanswered.

problems.title: Problem 5.2(d)
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
problems.prompt: Creditor lent debtor $5,000 in 2018 with required $6,000 repayment 2022; debtor files 2020, creditor claims full $6,000. Analyze unmatured interest discount and allowable petition-date balance; unanswered.

problems.title: Problem 5.2(e)
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
problems.prompt: Jan1 2012 landlord leased old military base 99 years at $100k annual; tenant repudiated Dec31 2019 with no rent arrears; Jan1 2020 Chapter 7; landlord immediately relet for remaining 91 years at $50k/year. Compute statutory §502(b)(6) months and compare actual mitigated damages; unanswered.

problems.title: Problem 5.2(f)
problems.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice (5th ed. 2021), uploaded Chapter 5 §B Allowance of Claims and Problems 5.2(a)-(f)
problems.prompt: Professional baseball player agreed 2018 to 10 years at $25m/year with 'Texas Strangers'; team discontinues operation, terminates contracts Jan1 2020 and files Chapter 7. Determine §502(b)(7) future damages cap and any other classification; unanswered.
